seo.title: Palace Sunday Illumination in Mysore (2026) | tabiji.ai
seo.metaDescription: Discover the best palace sunday illumination in Mysore for 2026 — curated picks with maps, hours, and insider tips.

hero.h1: 12 Best Stand transfixed as nearly 100,000 bulbs light up the Indo-Saracenic Mysore Palace every Sunday evening.
hero.subtitle: Experience the iconic Mysore Palace lighting and find the best nearby eateries to complete your magical Sunday evening.

picks.name: Hotel RRR
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A legendary establishment in Mysore, Hotel RRR is renowned for its authentic Andhra-style meals served on a banana leaf. Expect a spicy, flavorful culinary journey with unlimited rice, curries, pickles, and fiery gunpowder. It's a bustling, no-frills spot focused purely on exceptional food quality and taste.
picks.whatToOrder: The Special Andhra Meals (Thali) and the Chicken Biryani.
picks.insiderTip: Go during lunch hours for the full meal experience, or slightly before peak dinner time to avoid long queues. They don't take reservations.
picks.redditQuote: "Seriously, if you're in Mysore and don't eat at Hotel RRR, you've missed out. That Andhra thali is life-changing after seeing the palace lights!"

picks.name: Original Vinayaka Mylari (Dodda Gadiyara)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: This small, iconic eatery is a Mysore institution, famous for its incredibly soft, melt-in-your-mouth butter dosas. Served with a unique coconut chutney and a mild sagu (vegetable curry), the limited menu focuses on perfecting a few items. It's a humble spot offering an authentic taste of Mysore's breakfast culture.
picks.whatToOrder: Butter Masala Dosa and filter coffee.
picks.insiderTip: Seating is limited and often shared. Don't expect fancy ambiance; come for the unparalleled dosa experience. Cash payment is preferred.
picks.redditQuote: "The Original Vinayaka Mylari dosa after a Sunday evening at Mysore Palace is my perfect Mysore memory. It's truly legendary, so soft!"

picks.name: Gufha Restaurant
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Step into a unique dining experience at Gufha, a restaurant designed to resemble an ancient cave. The dark, intriguing ambiance, complete with stalactites and cave paintings, creates a memorable setting for their well-regarded North Indian and Continental dishes. It's perfect for a special evening out.
picks.whatToOrder: Butter Chicken, Paneer Tikka, and any of their signature mocktails.
picks.insiderTip: Make a reservation, especially on Sunday evenings, as its unique theme makes it very popular. The dim lighting adds to the ambiance but can make reading the menu a bit tricky.
picks.redditQuote: "We went to Gufha after seeing Mysore Palace lit up, and it was such a cool experience! The cave theme is awesome, and the food was surprisingly good."

picks.name: Om Shanthi Restaurant
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A popular vegetarian restaurant known for its clean, simple ambiance and delicious, wholesome South Indian meals. Om Shanthi is a local favorite for its consistent quality and generous portions, especially their daily changing thali. It's a great choice for a satisfying and authentic regional meal.
picks.whatToOrder: South Indian Thali (Meals) and the Masala Dosa.
picks.insiderTip: It can get crowded during lunch and dinner rushes, but the service is efficient. Perfect for a hearty, vegetarian meal before or after visiting the palace.
picks.redditQuote: "Om Shanthi is my go-to for a proper South Indian vegetarian meal in Mysore. Their thali is just perfect, no fuss, good food, just what you need before the palace."

picks.name: Oyster Bay
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Set in a sprawling garden, Oyster Bay offers a relaxed dining experience with both indoor and outdoor seating options. Their extensive multi-cuisine menu includes Indian, Chinese, and Continental dishes, making it a versatile choice for groups. The pleasant ambiance, especially in the evenings, is a major draw.
picks.whatToOrder: Their buffet spread often gets good reviews; from the à la carte, try the Tandoori Chicken or a pasta dish.
picks.insiderTip: Ideal for families or groups looking for a comfortable setting. The outdoor seating is lovely on pleasant evenings.
picks.redditQuote: "Oyster Bay has a great vibe, especially outside. We went after the Mysore Palace lighting, and it was nice to relax with some good food and open air."

picks.name: The Green Hotel
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A beautiful heritage hotel set in a former royal guesthouse, The Green Hotel is known for its commitment to eco-friendly practices and delightful organic cuisine. Its restaurant offers a serene atmosphere amidst lush gardens, serving a mix of European and Indian dishes made with locally sourced ingredients.
picks.whatToOrder: Their Fresh Salads, organic coffee, and home-baked desserts. The Indian main courses are also excellent.
picks.insiderTip: This is a perfect spot for a tranquil pre-palace lighting meal or a relaxing coffee break. Explore the gardens and the unique boutique shop.
picks.redditQuote: "The Green Hotel is a lovely escape. We had dinner there before heading to the Mysore Palace, and the organic food was so fresh, and the garden setting was just magical."

picks.name: Lalitha Mahal Palace Hotel Restaurant
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Dine like royalty in this majestic palace-turned-hotel, originally built for the Viceroy of India. The restaurant, with its grand interiors and high ceilings, offers a luxurious dining experience with a multi-cuisine menu, often featuring live classical music. It's an ideal choice for a celebratory or truly indulgent evening.
picks.whatToOrder: Their elaborate buffet or the traditional Indian thali.
picks.insiderTip: Dress smartly for the occasion to complement the opulent setting. Arrive a bit early to explore the palace grounds and enjoy the regal ambiance.
picks.redditQuote: "Splurged on dinner at the Lalitha Mahal Palace Hotel after seeing the Mysore Palace lit up, and it felt like part of the royal experience. Absolutely stunning!"

picks.name: By The Blue (at Grand Mercure Mysore)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Housed within the heritage-inspired Grand Mercure Mysore, By The Blue offers a sophisticated dining experience with a lovely poolside setting. Their multi-cuisine menu features Indian, Continental, and Asian dishes, prepared with a focus on fresh ingredients and elegant presentation.
picks.whatToOrder: Try their selection of kebabs or the well-curated Indian main courses.
picks.insiderTip: The poolside seating is particularly charming in the evenings. It's a great spot for a relaxed dinner after the palace spectacle, offering a touch of modern luxury.
picks.redditQuote: "The food at By The Blue at Grand Mercure was excellent, and the poolside vibe was so chill. A great way to unwind after the crowds at Mysore Palace."

picks.name: Old House
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Old House is a charming and popular spot for Italian and Continental fare in Mysore, known for its delicious wood-fired pizzas, fresh pastas, and cozy atmosphere. Housed in a beautifully restored old bungalow, it offers a welcome change of pace from traditional Indian cuisine.
picks.whatToOrder: Any of their wood-fired Pizzas, especially the Quattro Formaggi, and the Creamy Pesto Pasta.
picks.insiderTip: It can get busy, especially on weekends, so consider making a reservation. The outdoor seating in the garden is highly recommended.
picks.redditQuote: "If you're craving good pizza in Mysore after all the Indian food, Old House is the place. Their pizzas are legit, and it's a really cute spot for dinner."

picks.name: Indra Cafe's (Mysore Tiffins)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A quintessential Mysore experience, Indra Cafe's is a classic tiffin room, famed for its simple yet perfect South Indian breakfast and snack items. Known for their consistently good quality and quick service, it's a no-frills spot that locals frequent for authentic, freshly prepared items like idli, vada, and filter coffee.
picks.whatToOrder: Idli-Vada Combo, Kesari Bath, and a strong Filter Coffee.
picks.insiderTip: This is a perfect, quick, and very affordable stop for a snack or light meal before or after the palace lighting. Don't expect extensive seating, it's more of a stand-and-eat or quick turnover place.
picks.redditQuote: "After the Mysore Palace lights, grabbing a quick idli and coffee at Indra Cafe's is a tradition. It's cheap, fast, and exactly what you need."

picks.name: Depth N Brew
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A contemporary cafe that offers a vibrant and cozy ambiance, perfect for unwinding. Depth N Brew serves a variety of continental snacks, refreshing beverages, and delectable desserts. It's a popular hangout spot for younger crowds and those looking for a modern cafe experience.
picks.whatToOrder: Their special brews of coffee, waffles, and savory sandwiches.
picks.insiderTip: Great for a casual meet-up or a post-dinner dessert. They often have board games available, adding to the relaxed atmosphere.
picks.redditQuote: "Depth N Brew is my go-to for a good coffee and some dessert after a long day of sightseeing. Their waffles are amazing, perfect after the Mysore Palace crowds."

picks.name: Shikari (at The Green Hotel)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Situated within the beautiful grounds of The Green Hotel, Shikari offers an enchanting outdoor dining experience under the stars. Specializing in Indian cuisine, particularly North Indian and tandoori delights, it provides a romantic and peaceful setting away from the city's hustle.
picks.whatToOrder: Any of their Tandoori specialties or the traditional curries like Rogan Josh or Dal Makhani.
picks.insiderTip: This restaurant is seasonal and subject to weather, so check availability. It's perfect for a romantic dinner after witnessing the illuminated palace.
picks.redditQuote: "Shikari at the Green Hotel was such a beautiful place for dinner. Eating under the trees after seeing Mysore Palace lit up was pure magic. The curries were fantastic!"

faq.question: When does the Mysore Palace lighting happen?
faq.answer: The Mysore Palace is spectacularly lit up by nearly 100,000 bulbs every Sunday evening from 7:00 PM to 7:45 PM. It also gets illuminated during public holidays and special festivals like Dasara, often for extended durations. It's advisable to check the official palace website or local tourism guides for the most current schedule.

faq.question: Is there an entry fee to see the Mysore Palace lighting?
faq.answer: No, there is no separate entry fee to witness the exterior illumination of the Mysore Palace. You can view the lighting from the palace grounds or various vantage points around the perimeter. If you wish to enter the palace museum, there is a separate ticket required during daytime hours.

faq.question: What's the best time to arrive for the lighting?
faq.answer: It's recommended to arrive by 6:30 PM to secure a good viewing spot, especially during peak tourist season or festival days. This allows you to witness the transition from dusk to full illumination and capture some fantastic photographs without too much crowd hindrance.

faq.question: Where are the best viewing spots for the Mysore Palace lighting?
faq.answer: The main palace grounds offer the most direct and expansive view. Many visitors gather near the main entrance or the forecourt facing the illuminated facade. You can also find good vantage points from the surrounding roads, though these might be further away and often involve crowds.

faq.question: Are there any special considerations for visiting on a Sunday evening?
faq.answer: Yes, Sunday evenings are incredibly popular, so expect large crowds. Be mindful of your belongings and prepare for potential traffic around the palace area. Public restrooms are available on the palace grounds, and local vendors often sell snacks and drinks.

faq.question: Can I combine the palace lighting with a visit to the interior?
faq.answer: The palace interior museum is generally open from 10:00 AM to 5:30 PM daily, so you would need to visit it during the day. The lighting event starts after the interior visiting hours conclude. Plan your day to include both, perhaps visiting the interior in the late afternoon and then staying for the evening illumination.
